To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the complexity of rhythm can be measured using the entropy rate and that the Kolmogorv complexity is highly correlated with explicit complexity judgments.

entropy rate and Kolmogorv complexity are correlated with implicit and expicit judgments of rhythm complexity and that the effect of musical training on rhythm perception is mediated by the entropy rate.

entropy rate is correlated with implicit and with explicit judgments of rhythm complexity, Kolmogoro complexity is correlated with explicit judgments of rhythmic complexity, and scores on an implicit task are correlated with self-assessed musical perceptual ability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perceptual validity of measures of rhythm complexity.
the perceptual validity of information-theoretic measures of rhythm complexity.
the development of a perceptually valid complexity measure, and with the investigation of the role of expertise in rhythm perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
entropy rate and Kolmogoroff complexity are both valid measures of rhythmic complexity, with the first being the most valid measure.

entropy rate and Kolmogorv complexity, and possibly also the other complexity measures, are valid measures of rhythm complexity, and that the effect of musical training on rhythm perception is mediated by the ability to identify patterns.
the entropy rate measure is the most reliable and accurate measure of rhythm complexity in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the informationtheoretic measures of entropy rate and Kolmogoroff complexity, as well as self-assessed musical abilities are good predictors of rhythm perception.
the informationtheoretic measure of entropy rate is the best predictor of human rhythm complexity judgments.
entropy rate and musical expertise are important factors for the perception of rhythm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
entropy rate is an effective measure of the perceptual complexity of rhythmic patterns.
the information-theoretic approach to rhythm complexity is promising, and that it can be used as a basis for the development of more sophisticated models of rhythm complexity.
information theory can be a useful tool for the study of rhythm perception.
